messages.subject: problems with the "copy" feature
parts:
Dear INLA users,

I am trying to implement the following two likelihoods model in INLA:

x = Intercept_x + Slope_x * time + error
y = Intercept_y + Slope_y * time + beta*(Intercept_x + Slope_x*time) + error

where the linear predictor of x is copied in the linear predictor of y, scaling the effects with a new parameter beta estimated by INLA from the data.

I wrote the following code to do so:

fixed.effects <- list(Intercept_y = c(rep(NA, N_obs), rep(1, N_obs)),
                        t_y = c(rep(NA, N_obs), data$t),
                       
                        t = c(data$t, data$t))
 
random.effects <- list(Intercept_x = c(rep(1, N_obs), rep(NA, N_obs)),
                          t_x = c(rep(1, N_obs), rep(NA, N_obs)),
                         
                          Intercept_x_scaled = c(rep(NA, N_obs), rep(1, N_obs)),
                          t_x_scaled = c(rep(NA, N_obs), rep(1, N_obs)))
 
 
INLA_data <- c(fixed.effects, random.effects)
INLA_data$Y <- list(c(data$x, rep(NA, N_obs)),
                      c(rep(NA, N_obs), data$y))
 
INLA_formula = Y ~ -1 +
    # fixed effects of x 
    f(Intercept_x) + f(t_x, t) +
    # scaled fixed effects of x
    f(Intercept_x_scaled, copy = "Intercept_x", hyper = list(beta = list(fixed=FALSE))) +
    f(t_x_scaled, t, copy = "t_x", same.as = 'Intercept_x_scaled', hyper = list(beta = list(fixed=FALSE))) +
    # fixed effects of y
    Intercept_y + t_y
 

M2 <- inla(INLA_formula, family = c("gaussian","gaussian"), data = INLA_data)


I think that the structure of the code is correct, but looking at the results more in detail it seems to me that the copy feature is not really working in the Intercept.
Here below you can see the results of the Intercept_x and Slope_x scaled and not.

> M2$summary.hyperpar mean Precision for the Gaussian observations 0.30163126 Precision for the Gaussian observations[2] 0.01130564 Precision for Intercept_x 0.03346231 Precision for t_x 104.90106577 Beta for Intercept_x_scaled 1.05396431
> M2$summary.random$Intercept_x ID mean 1 1 10.20079 > M2$summary.random$Intercept_x_scaled ID mean
1 1 1.799346

> M2$summary.random$t_x ID mean 1 1 -0.163891 > M2$summary.random$t_x_scaled ID mean 1 1 -0.176995


As you can see, the posterior mean of the beta parameter is 1.0539. Thus, following the definition given in Section 6.5.1 in the "Bayesian inference with INLA" book, the estimates of the slopes t_x are almost identical, with a little difference given by the tiny added noise. The scaled intercept, instead, is not equal to beta*intercept_x + noise. 

Do you know what could be the problem? Changing the prior or working with the initial values does not seem to work.

Thanks in advance,
Chiara

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with the "copy" feature
parts:
with this model you can use the 'intslope' model, see

inla.doc('intslope')

then you can just add a copy of that one for the second part

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with the "copy" feature
parts:
Hi Dr. Rue,

if I understood right, the "intslope" model is perfect with correlated random effects. However, in my model I want the intercept and the slope fixed, thus not correlated. My bad, I did not specify that in the previous comment. I considered the parameters as random in the INLA formulation because was the only way to use the "copy" feature. Is there a way to use the "intslope" model assuming independence between the coefficients? 

I hope I did not leave anything out, but I could not find any information on it in the docs.

Thanks in advance,
Chiara

Il giorno mercoledì 16 agosto 2023 alle 23:06:03 UTC+2 Helpdesk (Haavard Rue) ha scritto:

with this model you can use the 'intslope' model, see

inla.doc('intslope')

then you can just add a copy of that one for the second part

parts:
if

y_i = a + b *x_i + noise
yy_i = beta * (a + b * x_i) + noise

and 'a' and 'b' is fixed, then with

off = a + b * x_i

but this is just

y ~ -1 + offset(off)
yy ~ -1 + off

right?????????

and then you can add an 'intslope' if you need another one?
